summary: The plan faithfully identifies the narrow Python allocation path, its production effects, and its limits as a reproduction of a full DRP launch. No blocking findings. One minor clarification would improve socket isolation and teardown accounting.
checks: Read the original task transfer, review contract, findings report, preserved issue and deployment evidence.
Verified Piranha4 constructor → BEBDetector init/init_feb and Collection Alloc → PGPDetectorApp → BEBDetector connectionInfo → Python call chain.
Verified synthetic allocation schema, insertion-order supervisor election, exact hostname/PID requirements, worker count, fixed barrier ports, and unbounded waits.
Verified startup escape/SPF/GCP commands precede allocation and remain active with enableConfig=False.
Verified timing setup and StopRun effects, distinct startup/allocation/CPA/VT/VV phases, parser stride and prompt conditions.
Checked fresh-process trial design, capture timing and bounded buffers, cleanup/watchdog requirements, production exclusivity, and phase-specific acceptance criteria.
Confirmed statistical estimates are explicitly conditional and paired-camera correlation is acknowledged.
limitations: Review was local and read-only; no imports of hardware dependencies, device access, runtime tests, or external-service calls were performed.
The coordinator's snapshot hash validation and additional successful-Alloc log checks were not independently repeated.
Source supports path feasibility; production race fidelity, callback instrumentation effects, and cleanup behavior still require the later implementation review and authorized hardware validation.

findings.evidence: The isolation discussion names barrier ports 5561/5562, but unchanged ClinkDevRoot also defaults zmqSrvEn=True and constructs pr.interfaces.ZmqServer(root=self, addr='*', port=0) (preserved ClinkDevRoot.py:55,85–88). The FZP launch excerpt records ports 9099–9101. Thus direct Python also starts a PyRogue server on dynamically selected ports.
findings.requested_change: Explicitly include the PyRogue server in the baseline side effects: record each child's assigned ports, avoid attaching GUI/VirtualClient clients during the baseline, and verify those listeners disappear during teardown. Preserve the deployed default unless a separately labeled experiment deliberately changes it.
